verses.1: The Bull of the Waters hath been let go; the heavenly fires have been let go.
verses.2: Breaking, breaking down, crushing, crushing to pieces,
verses.3: Mroka, mind-destroying, rooting up, consuming, ruiner of the soul, ruiner of the body.
verses.4: Here I let him go: thou washest me clean of him.
verses.5: With this we let him loose who hates us and whom we hate.
verses.6: Thou art in front of the waters. I let loose your sea.
verses.7: I let loose the Agni who is within the waters, Mroka the uprooter, the destroyer of the body.
verses.8: Your Agni who entered into the waters, even he here is that very dread of yours.
verses.9: May he anoint you with Indra's own mighty power!
verses.10: May stainless waters cleanse us from defilement.
verses.11: May they carry sin away from us, may they carry away from us the evil dream.
verses.12: Look on me with a friendly eye, O, Waters, and touch my skin with your auspicious body.
verses.13: We call the gracious Fires that dwell in waters. Goddesses, grant me princely power and splendour.
verses.14: Away from distasteful food, strength and sweet speech,
verses.15: Are pleasant. May I obtain a pleasant voice.
verses.16: I have invoked the Protector; I have invoked his protection.
verses.17: Quick of hearing are mine ears; mine ears hear what is good- Fain would I hear a pleasant sound.
verses.18: Let not good hearing and overhearing fail the Eagle's eye, the undecaying light.
verses.19: Thou art the couch of the Rishis. Let worship be paid to the divine couch.
verses.20: I am the head of riches. Fain would I be the head of mine equals.
verses.21: Let not Ruja and Vena desert me. Let not the Head and the Preserver forsake me.
verses.22: Let not the Boiler and the Cup fail tme: let not the Supporter and the Sustainer abandon me.
verses.23: Let not Unyoking and the Moist-fellied car desert me: let not the Sender of Moisture and Matarisvan forsake me.
verses.24: Brihaspati is my soul, he who is called the Friend of man, dear to my heart.
verses.25: My heart is free from sorrow; spacious is my dwelling-place. I am the sea in capacity.
verses.26: I am the:centre of riches. Fain would I be the centre of mine equals.
verses.27: Pleasant art thou to sit by one, a mother: immortal among mortals.
verses.28: Let not inward breath desert me; let not outward breath depart and leave me.
verses.29: Let Surya protect me from Day, Agni from Earth, Vayu from Firmament, Yama from men, Sarasvati from dwellers on the earth.
verses.30: Let not outward and inward breath fail me. Be not thou destructive among the men.
verses.31: Propitious to-day be dawns and evenings. May I drink water with all my people safe around me.
verses.32: Mighty are ye, domestic creatures. May Mitra-Varuna stand beside me. May Agni give me inward and outward breath. May,he give me ability.
verses.33: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of Grahi, the minister of Yama. Thou art the Ender, thou art Death. As such, O Sleep, we know thee well. As such preserve us from the evil dream.
verses.34: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of Destruction, the minister of Yama, etc. (as in verse 1).
verses.35: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of Misery, etc.
verses.36: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of Disappearance, etc.
verses.37: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of Defeat etc.
verses.38: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of the sisters of the Gods, the minister of Yama. Thou art the Ender, thou are Death. As such, O Sleep, we know thee well. As such, preserve us from the evil dream.
verses.41: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of Destruction, the minister of Yama, etc. (as in verse 1).
verses.42: We know thine origin, O Sleep. Thou art the son of Misery, etc.
verses.43: Now have we conquered and obtained: we have been freed from sin to-day.
verses.44: Let Morning with her light dispel that evil dream that frightened us.
verses.45: Bear that away to him who hates, away to him who curses us.
verses.46: To him whom we abhor, to him who hates us do we send it hence.
verses.47: May the Goddess Dawn in accord with Speech, and the Goddess Speech in accord with Dawn,
verses.48: The Lord of Dawn in accord with the Lord of Speech and the Lord of Speech in accord with the Lord of Dawn,
verses.49: Carry away to Such-an-one niggard fiends, hostile demons, and Sadanvas,
verses.51: Evil day-dream, evil dream in sleep,
verses.52: Wishes for boons that will not come, thoughts of poverty, the snares of the Druh who never releases.
verses.53: This, O Agni, let the Gods bear off to Such-an-one that he may be a fragile good-for-nothing eunuch.
verses.54: Herewith I pierce this man. With poverty I pierce him. With disappearance I pierce him. With defeat I pierce him. With Grahi I pierce him. With darkness I pierce him.
verses.55: I summon him with the awful cruel orders of the Gods.
verses.56: I place him between Vaisvanara's jaws.
verses.57: Thus or otherwise let her swallow him up.
verses.58: Him who hates us may his soul hate, and may he whom we hate hate himself.
verses.59: We scorch out of heaven and earth and firmament the man who hates us.
verses.61: Here I wipe away the evil dream on the descendant of Such-anone, son of Such-a-woman.
verses.62: Whatsoever I have met with, whether at dusk or during early night,
verses.63: Whether waking or sleeping, whether by day or by night.
verses.64: Whether I meet with it day by day, from that do I bribe him away.
verses.65: Slay him; rejoice in this; crush his ribs.
verses.66: Let him not live. Let the breath of life forsake him.
verses.67: Whatever we have gained, whatever hath accrued to us, our Right, our energy, our Devotion, our heavenly light, our sacrifice, our domestic animals, our offspring, our men,--from all share herein we exclude Such-an-one, descendant of Suchan-one, son of Such-a-woman. Let him not be freed from the noose of Grahi. Here I bind up his splendour, his energy, his vital breath, his life, and cast him down beneath me.
verses.68: Whatever we have gained, etc. (as in verse 1). Let him not be freed from the noose of Nirriti, etc.
verses.69: Whatever we have gained, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of misery, etc.
verses.70: Whatever we have gained, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of disappearance, etc.
verses.71: Whatever we have gained, etc. (as in verse 1). Let him not be freed from the noose of Nirriti, etc.
verses.72: Whatever we have gained, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of misery, etc.

verses.76: Whatever we have gained, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of Brihaspati, etc.
verses.77: Whatever we have gained, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of Prajapati, etc.
verses.78: Whatever we have gained, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Rishis, etc.
verses.79: Whatever we have gained, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Rishis' children, etc.
verses.80: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Angirases, etc.
verses.81: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Angirases, etc.
verses.82: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Atharvans, etc.
verses.83: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Atharvans, etc.
verses.84: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Trees, etc.
verses.85: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of Shrubs, etc.
verses.86: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Seasons, etc.
verses.87: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Season-groups, etc.
verses.88: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Months, etc.
verses.89: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of the Halfmonths, etc.
verses.90: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of Day and Night, etc.
verses.91: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of continued Day, etc.
verses.92: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of Heaven and Earth, etc.
verses.93: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of Indra- Agni, etc.
verses.94: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of Mitra- Varuna, etc.
verses.95: Whatever, etc. Let him not be freed from the noose of King Varuna, etc.
verses.96: Whatever we have gained, whatever hath accrued to us, our Right, our energy, our Devotion, our heavenly light, our sacrifice, our domestic animals, our offspring, our men,
verses.97: --from all share herein we exclude Such-as-one, descendant of Suchan-one, son of Such-a-woman.
verses.98: Let him not be freed from the fetter and noose of Death.
verses.99: Here I bind up his splendour, his energy, his vital breath, his life, and cast him down beneath me.
verses.100: Ours is superior place and ours is conquest: may I in all fights tread down spite and malice.
verses.101: This word hath Agni, this hath Soma spoken. May Pushan set me in the world of virtue.
verses.102: We have come to the light of heaven; to the light of heaven have we come: we have united with the light of Surya.
verses.103: Sacrifice is fraught with wealth for the increase of prosperity. I would win riches; fain would I be wealthy. Do thou bestow wealth upon me.
